data.turoyo: I arnuwo emo: "Dmax gəmdarmənalla." Daməx u baran. Aṯi u zoġo, nqəzle i ʕayno ḥreto.
data.translation: Der Hase aber sagte: "Lege dich nieder, ich will dein Auge heilen." Als der Widder sich niederlegte, kam der Hahn wieder und pickte ihm das andere Auge aus;

rationale: First Preterit box: explicit bird subject and a zero-marked affected eye. The surrounding ram context makes the possessed body part interpretable.

data.turoyo: Huwe kloṭəʕ w i bumo w i bumo knəqzo. Axile lu taʕlo u ḥawdal.
data.translation: Er leckte und die Eule pickte, so frass er den ganzen Brei,

rationale: Thin Infectum cell (1 existing): third-person feminine knəqzo with an explicit owl subject contrasts with inherited first-person feminine knuqzono. Preserve the repeated w i bumo.

summary: The new Preterit nqəzle confirms the printed base form. Its overt patient i ʕayno ḥreto contrasts with the objectless food-pecking Infectum; the outcome “peck out an eye” follows from the affected body part and context, not an independently demonstrated sense.
Feminine -o in knəqzo and -ono in knəqzono correspond to the owl as subject. The patient can be omitted when food is recoverable from the discourse.
Licking versus pecking is the fable’s contrast between two animals and feeding methods. It does not demonstrate a fixed collocation or another sense.
The duplicated w i bumo in PrS 82/5 is copied exactly; no normalization or edition repair is attempted.

Confirm the reference concordance between prs 238/37 and PrS 82/6; the inherited first-person example is retained rather than duplicated or recited under a silently changed reference.
